comment: An INSTANCE member's OWN signature carries a dictionary requirement, and the analyzer was reading it and then throwing it away. The defect was not a missing branch: the declaration pass filed every signature in `ctx.signatures` under a derived STRING key, and for an instance member the two passes derived DIFFERENT strings — `|::cmp` in the declaration pass, which does not know the instance's target, against `|[!a]::cmp` in the emitting pass, which is standing in the instance's scope. The lookup missed, `applySignature` never ran, and the signature's types and its class context were discarded. 20 class_context sites at PROD published no edge at all for this reason. Both passes now index by the node's own id (`signaturesByNode`). The label stays `references`: a dictionary requirement is a type the member needs, which is what every other lane's `references` means, and re-labelling it `extends` would assert a supertype Clean does not have.

expectSymbols.name: Cmp
expectSymbols.comment: a class_declaration publishes as an Interface

expectSymbols.name: [!a]::instance
expectSymbols.comment: the instance container, NAMESPACED under its target. The target is a strict-LIST type expression, which is why the bare form could never have been a declaration of anything: no symbol in any file is named `[!a]`. The members' owner is still `[!a]`, so the `references from [!a]` row below is unchanged.

expectSymbols.name: [!a!]::instance
expectSymbols.comment: a second instance of the SAME class, so `cmp` is declared twice under two owners — and the two containers are two names, because the two targets differ

expectSymbols.name: moduleLevel
expectSymbols.comment: the module-scope control: this form has always read and must keep reading

expectRelationships.comment: THE TARGET ROW. The instance member's own `| Ord a`, which published nothing before the per-node index
the same name under a DIFFERENT owner. A dedupe keyed on (owner,name) would keep line 34's and lose this one
a member whose context names a class declared in ANOTHER file. The edge is still true and is still `references` — dropping it is the defect; promoting it to `overrides` would be a different defect
a where-LOCAL signature inside an instance member's body: the `local_binding` grandparent, one of the 6 unread sites
the control in the positive direction: module scope read this before the change and must still read it
the INSTANCE's own context, `instance_context`, which was never affected — kept so a regression in it is caught here too
`declared_type` from the same unread signature: L62's `size` has a type and NO class context, which is the control in the negative direction

expectRelationshipCount.comment: two instance members constrain on `Ord` at L34 and L53. Exactly 2 — not 1 (a dedupe would collapse them) and not 3 (the instance's own context is a different source)

forbidRelationships.comment: the INSTANCE's context is anchored on the instance line and names the instance's target as source. Line 32 is `[!a] -> Ord`, and no edge may claim the member `cmp` is on that line
the negative control: `size :: !Int -> Int` names no class, so nothing may be invented for it. An absence that becomes an edge is a fabrication
the same absence, the other class
`Ord` is a CLASS, not a class member. The `overrides` rule pairs a member with its class's member of the same name and nothing else may borrow the type
a dictionary requirement is a reference to a class, never a construction of one
`implements` belongs to the INSTANCE (`[!a] -> Cmp`), never to a member
naming a class in a type position is a reference, not a call
the ruled type. Nothing in this file may produce one — see script/m14/clean-ruled.ts
